verdicts.evidence: paper/PAPER.md:146–162 separates empty-cell support from numerical marginals and adds the facial-set characterization and LP certificates. Independent recomputation forces probabilities of 000 and 111 to zero in the referee’s six-profile example. The complete rerun reproduces the three- and four-issue enumeration counts and certificate checks.

paper/PAPER.md:9, 19, 55 and 78–80 restrict pairwise completeness to unrestricted product domains. Lines 204–206 explicitly separate commitment compatibility from empirical correlations and respondent distances; the unsupported survey-map inference is removed.

paper/PAPER.md:174 and simulation/atlas/empirical.py:190–215 apply researcher and repeat-submission screening. Independent raw-CSV counts reproduce 307 submissions, 18 repeat submissions, 232 eligible respondents, 166 eligible conference attendees and 223 complete position respondents. Both derived datasets rebuild to their recorded hashes.

simulation/atlas/empirical.py:32–49 replaces the independent-fold variance with s²(1/J + n_test/n_train) and a Student-t interval. paper/PAPER.md:176, 180, 188 and 190 identify the corrected estimates and cite Nadeau and Bengio. The rerun reproduces corrected standard errors 0.06097547 and 0.17840947 for the two batteries.

paper/PAPER.md:176, 188 and 194 distinguish prespecified-triplet power from full-screening power. With 9,999 draws, the attainable p-value 0.0001 is below 0.05/165. empirical.py:384–473 reruns penalty selection, fitting, Monte Carlo testing and BH screening on simulated datasets. The independent rerun reproduces discovery of the trolley-sized planted effect in 0/100 datasets.

paper/PAPER.md:192–194 replaces exclusion with non-detection and limited sensitivity. All 165 simultaneous Wald intervals contain zero, and none excludes the trolley-sized interaction. Lines 194 and 210 say the effect would most likely have been missed; lines 200–212 qualify the proposed PhilPapers test by prespecification and multiplicity.

paper/PAPER.md:45–49 now requires Ω to belong to the class and closure under arbitrary intersections, ensuring the smallest containing set exists. It states the obstruction-free convention and explains why bounded open intervals violate the required hypothesis.
paper/PAPER.md:9 and 19 now attribute order n+1 to categorical answers together with implications. Table 1 and line 86 retain order one for implications alone.

new_problems.problem: The newly reported 8.25 is presented as an expected null count although calibration of the implemented p-values is unestablished. Label it as a nominal reference or estimate the expectation through simulation.
new_problems.evidence: empirical.py:332 sets expected_below_005_under_null = 0.05 * m. paper/PAPER.md:176 expressly states that calibration of the fitted-model Monte Carlo p-values was not established. The recorded product 165 × 0.05 supports the arithmetic, but not the asserted expectation.

claims_coverage.note: Checked the whole manuscript, including tables, captions and spelled-out numerical quantities, applying the requested exclusions. All 443 bound passages occur verbatim; all 171 computation claims match their recorded values, scaling and rounding. The abstract has 246 words. A complete scratch rerun passed all 34 tests and reproduced every substantive result exactly; differences were confined to Python-version metadata and timings. All recorded input/output hashes match.

source_claims.note: Inspected the finite-family Helly theorem on p. 102 of the [survey](https://www3.nd.edu/~andyp/teaching/2013SpringMath366/DanzerGruenbaumKlee.pdf). It supplies the d+1 bound; the standard simplex example supplies sharpness.
Inspected Definition 1.4 in [Averkov’s preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6179v3). It supports the identification, subject to the manuscript’s explicit convention for obstruction-free classes.
Inspected equation (3.1), stating invariance under taking intersections. [Averkov](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6179v3).

Inspected the products and axis-parallel-box discussion on p. 144. It supports the pairwise-intersection property used here. [Danzer et al.](https://www3.nd.edu/~andyp/teaching/2013SpringMath366/DanzerGruenbaumKlee.pdf).
Inspected Theorem 2.2: pairwise intersection suffices for axis-parallel boxes. [Amenta et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1508.07606v2).
Inspected [Amenta et al., Lemma 2.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1508.07606v2), stating Hoffman’s characterization. This checks the cited accessible presentation, not Hoffman’s original chapter.

Inspected Averkov’s lattice discussion and Remark 4.5. The lattice bound and unit-cell witness support the statement; Doignon’s original was not independently read. [Averkov](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6179v3).

Inspected Proposition 3.1 and the lattice discussion: convex restriction cannot increase the Helly number, and the unit-cell construction attains the grid bound. [Averkov](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.6179v3).
Inspected Lemma 2.6, relating the discrete Helly number to empty convex polytopes. [Amenta et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1508.07606v2).

Inspected p. 2 of [Heule and Scheucher’s preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.00737v1): the definition of h(k), Harborth’s h(5)=10, and Theorem 1 support the passage. This checks the declared secondary source, not Harborth’s original article.

Inspected Theorem 1 and its general-position hypothesis. It establishes the 30-point empty-hexagon threshold; I did not rerun the external computer-assisted proof. [Heule et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.00737v1).

Inspected the opening result and construction: arbitrarily large general-position sets without empty convex heptagons exist. [Horton](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/0E7C17D71D9FA4A08B265441FBEB32D7/S0008439500065176a.pdf/sets_with_no_empty_convex_7gons.pdf).

Inspected Theorem 2. The growth rate holds in expectation and with high probability for independent uniform points in a bounded convex planar region; those sampling conditions should remain explicit. [Balogh et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1206.0805v1).

Inspected Theorem 2.5 and the decidability statement. The equivalence is credited to Atserias; decidability is established separately, not by Theorem 2.5 alone. [Larose et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.2562).

Retrieved and read the [Econometric Society abstract](https://www.econometricsociety.org/publications/econometrica/1979/05/01/consistent-majority-rules-over-compact-sets-alternatives). It states the quota threshold for convex, continuous preferences on a compact convex domain. The revised passage includes these conditions.

Inspected Corollary 2: the uniform-quota consistency condition is exactly m > n − n/z under the paper’s agenda assumptions. [Dietrich and List](https://personal.lse.ac.uk/list/PDF-files/QuotaRules.pdf).

Inspected Section 3.3 on preference judgments and cycles. It supports the largest minimally inconsistent cycle and resulting quota threshold. [Dietrich and List](https://personal.lse.ac.uk/list/PDF-files/QuotaRules.pdf).

Inspected the implication-graph construction and Theorem 1, pp. 121–122. Mutual reachability of a literal and its negation characterizes unsatisfiability. [Aspvall et al.](https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~sbuss/CourseWeb/Math268_2007WS/2SAT.pdf).
Inspected the correlation analysis and factor-analysis discussion in the [author manuscript](https://consc.net/papers/survey.pdf). They support this description of the survey maps.
Inspected p. 12, following Table 3: contingency tables are stated to be available for all answer pairs on the survey site. [Bourget and Chalmers](https://consc.net/papers/survey.pdf).

Inspected Section 3.1. It reports no release of individual responses linked to demographics; this concerns the survey dataset, not the absence of all public individual answers. [Shi and Haupt](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.23575v2).
Inspected the evaluation of simulated philosophers and cross-question correlation structure. [Shi and Haupt](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.23575v2).

The publisher/Crossref abstract explicitly describes 100 philosophical questions. It does not supply the separate respondent count attributed to Shi. [Bourget and Chalmers](https://doi.org/10.3998/phimp.2109).
Inspected the abstract and survey description, explicitly giving N = 1,785. [Shi and Haupt](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.23575v2).

Inspected the bibliographic-coupling and UMAP methods. Shared citations supply similarity, and Figure 2 is a two-dimensional representation. [Noichl](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11229-019-02390-8.pdf).

The indexed abstract supports topic modelling during 1934–2015. This source covers 82 years; the sentence’s century-scale span is supported by co-cited Weatherson. [Malaterre et al.](https://doi.org/10.1086/704372).
Inspected the author’s introduction: topic models cover twelve journals during 1876–2013, supporting the century-scale description. [Weatherson](https://public.websites.umich.edu/~weath/lda/).
Inspected equations (5)–(6): multi-information decomposes into the sum of connected-information terms. [Schneidman et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/physics/0307072).

Inspected the ten-cell analysis and Figure 2 discussion. The pairwise model captures approximately 90% of multi-information. [Schneidman et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/q-bio/0512013).
Inspected the XOR example and Figure 1: pairwise mutual informations vanish while multi-information is one bit. [Schneidman et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/physics/0307072).

Inspected the indexed abstract describing generalized iterative scaling under linear constraints. It supports the method, not the manuscript’s independently computed sample size or estimates. [Darroch and Ratcliff](https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177692379).
Inspected Materials and Methods: the classic mode presents Switch, Loop and Footbridge in randomized order. [Awad et al.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7007553/).

Inspected the cross-country results: Switch exceeds Loop, which exceeds Footbridge, in every country. The manuscript’s particular percentages are its own reproduced calculations. [Awad et al.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7007553/).

Downloaded the [Yale repository scan](https://openyls.law.yale.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/2549174b-4728-45bf-bf64-01384116e48c/content). Inspected pp. 1395, 1402 and 1409: Foot is credited, and the loop and footbridge cases are presented.

Inspected Methods and Participants: recruitment focused on the 2018 and 2019 ASSC conferences, with other submissions also admitted. [Francken et al.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9374479/).

Inspected Section 2.5 and Definition 2: a minimal unsatisfiable subset becomes satisfiable when any member is removed. [Liffiton and Sakallah](https://markliffiton.com/publications/jar_liffiton_CAMUS.pdf).

Inspected the definition of minimally inconsistent subsets used in the quota-rule results. It matches the obstruction definition. [Dietrich and List](https://personal.lse.ac.uk/list/PDF-files/QuotaRules.pdf).
Inspected Theorem 4.4: diagnoses are precisely minimal hitting sets of conflict sets. [Reiter](https://www.cs.ru.nl/~peterl/teaching/KeR/reiter.pdf).

Inspected Section 3 and Theorem 1: minimal correction subsets and minimal unsatisfiable subsets are hitting-set duals. [Liffiton and Sakallah](https://markliffiton.com/publications/jar_liffiton_CAMUS.pdf).

Inspected Theorem 2.1 and the Horn, bijunctive and affine definitions. The operation-based formulation is supplied by co-cited Chen, not stated in this form by Schaefer. [Original paper](https://www.khoury.northeastern.edu/home/lieber/courses/csg260/f06/materials/papers/max-sat/p216-schaefer.pdf).
Inspected Theorem 3.20 and the polymorphism presentation: conjunction, majority and ternary parity give the claimed preservation and tractability cases. [Chen](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0611018).
Inspected Proposition 1 and its implication-path proof, giving the 4n−2 upper bound. [Lee](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v16i1n3/pdf).

Inspected the construction and lower bound for fixed k ≥ 3. It supplies Ω(n^k); the matching counting upper bound is the manuscript’s elementary inference. [Lee](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v16i1n3/pdf).

Inspected Section 6.1.2, Theorem 24 and its proof, pp. 28–29 of [Feder and Vardi’s manuscript](https://www.cs.rice.edu/~vardi/papers/stoc93rj.pdf). Inspected Theorem 24: the l-Helly property, near-unanimity polymorphisms and strict width are related as claimed in this setting. [Feder and Vardi](https://www.cs.rice.edu/~vardi/papers/stoc93rj.pdf).

contribution_after.assessment: The paper connects established Helly, constraint-satisfaction, marginal-polytope and connected-information results around a clear question about philosophical maps. Its exhaustive support comparisons and public-data reanalyses add reproducible numerical results, while the principal structural characterizations are established theory now credited appropriately.

summary: All eight referee findings are closed; one minor null-count interpretation needs correction. The full rerun passed 34 tests and reproduced every substantive result. All six added references match Crossref; 68 prior source verdicts are retained unchanged and the remaining claim is supported. Numerical coverage is complete and all 25 pages are visually clean. No prohibited self-reference or availability-section defect was found.
